newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Talks fail to resolve Colombia port strike.
newsitem.headline: Talks fail to resolve Colombia port strike.

text.p: Talks between dock workers, cargo operators and ship owners broke up early Wednesday without any agreement on the eight-day-old strike that has paralyzed Colombia's main Pacific coast port, a union leader said.

More than 11 hours of negotiations failed to break the deadlock in the port of Buenaventura stoppage, which has blocked more than 300,000 60-kg bags of coffee exports and 27,000 tonnes of sugar exports.

Nelson Amaya, regional head of the Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT), to which the main dockers' union is affiliated, said talks were scheduled to resume about 11 local(1600 GMT) Wednesday in the nearby provincial capital Cali. He blamed the cargo owners and operators for intransigence over a basic list of workers' demands.
"Things are tough. The ship and cargo owners and the cargo handling operators are negotiating hard and just won't shift their position," Amaya said.

Signs emerged late Tuesday that a deal was about to be reached that would almost double the tariffs dock workers are paid for unloading each tonne of cargo from the current 233 pesos to 425 pesos (about U.S. 40 cents). The accord would also have granted social security, sickness and injury benefits and meal allowances to dockers, who currently earn an average of about $80 per month.
But positions appeared to harden after a late break for food, forcing the suspension of negotiations in the early hours Wednesday.
It is estimated that the strike is costing the port of Buenaventura $500,000 for every day it continues, as well as paralyzing key exports.
Hopes emerged for an early end to the strike last Thursday but dockers rejected an agreement which their representatives had hammered out with the other parties in the dispute.
